title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.en: Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
units.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.
units.idiomatic: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.

units.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
units.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
units.idiomatic: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

units.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
units.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.
units.idiomatic: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.

units.zh: 豆盧革
units.literal: Dou Luge
units.idiomatic: Dou Luge

units.zh: 豆盧革，父瓚，唐舒州刺史。
units.literal: Dou Luge—his father Zan had been Tang prefect of Shu Prefecture.
units.idiomatic: Dou Luge’s father Zan had served Tang as prefect of Shu.

units.zh: 豆盧為世名族，唐末天下亂，革避地之中山，唐亡，為王處直掌書記。
units.literal: The Dou Lu were a famous clan of the age. At the end of Tang, when the realm was in chaos, Ge took refuge in Zhongshan. After Tang fell he served Wang Chuzhi as chief secretary.
units.idiomatic: The Dou Lu were a great house. When Tang collapsed into chaos, Ge fled to Zhongshan. After the dynasty fell he became chief secretary to Wang Chuzhi.

units.zh: 仁者之勇，何其壯也！」
units.literal: The courage of the humane—how mighty!”
units.idiomatic: The courage of the humane—how mighty!”

units.zh: 張文禮弒王镕，莊宗遣嗣昭討之。
units.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong. Zhuangzong sent Sizhao to suppress him.
units.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong. Zhuangzong sent Sizhao against him.

units.zh: 嗣昭戰歿，圜代將其軍，號令嚴肅。
units.literal: Sizhao died in battle. Huan took command of his army with strict discipline.
units.idiomatic: Sizhao fell in battle. Huan took his army and kept iron discipline.

units.zh: 朱宣
units.literal: Zhu Xuan
units.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan

units.literal: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉
units.idiomatic: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉

units.zh: 朱宣，宋州下邑人也。
units.literal: Zhu Xuan was a native of Xiayi in Song prefecture.
units.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan came from Xiayi in Songzhou.

units.zh: 京師大風拔木，末帝大懼，從官相顧而泣，末帝乃還東都，遂不果郊。
units.literal: A great wind in the capital uprooted trees. The Last Emperor was greatly afraid; attendants looked at one another and wept. He returned to the eastern capital and the suburban sacrifice was never carried out.
units.idiomatic: A gale uprooted trees in the capital. The Last Emperor panicked; courtiers wept at one another. He turned back to the eastern capital and never performed the suburban rite.

units.zh: 鎮州張文禮殺王镕，使人告梁曰：「臣已北召契丹，願梁以兵萬人出德、棣州，則晉兵憊矣。」
units.literal: Zhang Wenli of Zhen Prefecture killed Wang Rong and sent word to Liang: “Your servant has already summoned Khitan from the north; if Liang will march ten thousand men out of De and Di prefectures, the Jin army will be exhausted.”
units.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli of Zhen murdered Wang Rong and wrote Liang: “I have called Khitan from the north. Send ten thousand men from De and Di, and Jin will break.”

units.zh: 敬翔以為然，巖與漢傑皆以為不可，乃止。
units.literal: Jing Xiang thought it right, but Yan and Hanjie both said it could not be done, and so it stopped.
units.idiomatic: Jing Xiang agreed; Yan and Hanjie refused, and nothing was done.

title.en: Volume 147 Biographies 34: Zhang Rou, Shi Tianni, Shi Tianxiang
title.raw: 卷一百四十七 列傳第三十四: 張柔 史天倪 史天祥 Volume 147 Biographies 34: Zhang Rou, Shi Tianni, Shi Tianxiang

units.zh: 張柔，字德剛，易州定興人，世力農。
units.literal: Zhang Rou, style name Degang, was a native of Dingxing in Yizhou; his family for generations labored as farmers.
units.idiomatic: Zhang Rou, styled Degang, came from Dingxing in Yizhou. His family had farmed the land for generations.

units.zh: 柔少慷慨，尚氣節，善騎射，以豪俠稱。
units.literal: In his youth Rou was magnanimous, esteemed integrity and honor, excelled at mounted archery, and was known as a bold hero.
units.idiomatic: As a young man Rou was open-handed and chivalrous, prized loyalty and courage, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and famed as a gallant free spirit.

units.zh: 金貞祐間，河北盜起，柔聚族黨保西山東流寨，選壯士，結隊伍以自衛，盜不敢犯。
units.literal: During the Jinyou era of Jin, bandits rose in Hebei. Rou gathered his clan to hold Dongliu Stockade in the Western Hills, selected strong men, formed companies for self-defense, and bandits did not dare molest them.
units.idiomatic: In the Jinyou reign of the Jin, brigands spread across Hebei. Rou rallied his kinsmen to defend Dongliu Stockade in the Western Hills, picked stalwart fighters, and organized armed bands for protection so that raiders dared not trouble them.

units.zh: 下令：敢有剽虜者，以軍法從事。
units.literal: He issued an order: whoever dares plunder shall be dealt with by military law.
units.idiomatic: He issued an order: anyone who plunders will be dealt with under military law.

units.zh: 辛巳，金懷州元帥王榮、潞州元帥裴守謙、澤州太守王珍皆以城降。
units.literal: On the day xinsi the Jin commanders Wang Rong of Huaizhou, Pei Shouqian of Luzhou, and Defender Wang Zhen of Zezhou all surrendered their cities.
units.idiomatic: On xinsi day the Jin commanders Wang Rong of Huaizhou, Pei Shouqian of Luzhou, and Wang Zhen, defender of Zezhou, all surrendered their cities.

units.zh: 壬午，攻濟南水寨，破之。
units.literal: On the day renwu he attacked the Jinan river stockade and broke it.
units.idiomatic: On renwu day he attacked the Jinan river stockade and captured it.

units.zh: 卷第一百三十六
units.literal: Volume 136
units.idiomatic: Volume 136

units.zh: 【齊紀二】 起閼逢困敦，盡屠維大荒落，凡六年。
units.literal: [Qi Records 2] From Efou Kundun through Tuxi Dahuangluo, six years in all.
units.idiomatic: [Qi Records 2] From Shangzhang Zhixu through Xuanyi Dunzang—six years in all.

units.zh: 開西邸，多聚古人器服以充之。
units.literal: He opened the Western Lodge and gathered many ancient vessels and vestments to fill it.
units.idiomatic: He opened the Western Lodge and filled it with antiquities—vessels and vestments from former ages.

units.zh: 記室參軍范雲、蕭琛、樂安任昉、法曹參軍王融、衛軍東閣祭酒蕭衍、鎮西功曹謝朓、步兵校尉沈約、揚州秀才吳郡陸倕，並以文學，尤見親待，號曰八友。
units.literal: Recorder-General Fan Yun, Xiao Chen, Le'an Ren Fang, Legal Affairs Officer Wang Rong, Eastern Pavilion Libationer of the Guards Army Xiao Yan, Merit Officer of the West Garrison Xie Tiao, Footsoldier Commandant Shen Yue, and Yangzhou Presented Scholar Lu Chun of Wu Commandery—all famed for letters and especially favored—were called the Eight Friends.
units.idiomatic: Recorder-General Fan Yun, Xiao Chen, Ren Fang of Le'an, Legal Affairs Officer Wang Rong, Eastern Pavilion Libationer Xiao Yan, West Garrison merit officer Xie Tiao, Footsoldier Commandant Shen Yue, and presented scholar Lu Chun of Wu—all celebrated for literature and especially cherished—were known as the Eight Friends.

units.zh: 法曹參軍柳惲、太學博士王僧孺、南徐州秀才濟陽江革、尚書殿中郎范縝、會稽孔休源亦預焉。
units.literal: Legal Affairs Officer Liu Yun, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Sengru, South Xuzhou Presented Scholar Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji also took part.
units.idiomatic: Liu Yun, Wang Sengru, Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji were among them as well.

units.zh: 惲，元景之從孫；
units.literal: Yun was a grandnephew of Yuanjing;
units.idiomatic: Yun was a grandnephew of Yuanjing;

units.zh: 融，僧達之孫；
units.literal: Rong was a grandson of Sengda;
units.idiomatic: Rong was a grandson of Sengda;

units.zh: 衍，順之之子；
units.literal: Yan was a son of Shunzhi;
units.idiomatic: Yan was a son of Shunzhi;

units.zh: 知其先祖神靈所在，而不能殺身以從之！」
units.literal: You know where the spirits of your ancestors abide, yet cannot kill yourself to follow them!"
units.idiomatic: You know where your ancestors' spirits abide, yet you cannot kill yourself to join them!"

units.zh: 子良使王融謂之曰：「以卿才美，何患不至中書郎；
units.literal: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent and beauty, why worry that you will not reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;
units.idiomatic: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent, why should you fail to reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;

units.zh: 而故乖剌為此論，甚可惜也！
units.literal: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how very regrettable!
units.idiomatic: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how regrettable!

title.en: Volume 8 Book of Later Liang 8: Later Emperors Annals 1
title.raw: 卷八 梁書8: 末帝本紀上 Volume 8 Book of Later Liang 8: Later Emperors Annals 1

units.zh: 末帝，諱瑱，初名友貞，及即位，改名鍠，貞明中又改今諱。
units.literal: The Last Emperor, taboo name Zhen, was originally named Youzhen; on taking the throne he changed his name to Huang, and in Zhenming again changed to his present taboo name.
units.idiomatic: The Last Emperor, taboo name Zhen, was originally Youzhen; on accession he took the name Huang, and in Zhenming changed to his present taboo name.

units.zh: 太祖第四子也。
units.literal: He was Taizu's fourth son.
units.idiomatic: He was Taizu's fourth son.

units.zh: 母曰元貞皇后張氏。
units.literal: His mother was Empress Yuanzhen, née Zhang.
units.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Yuanzhen (Zhang).

units.zh: 己丑，魏博軍亂，囚節度使賀德倫。
units.literal: On jichou the Weibo army mutinied and imprisoned Military Commissioner He Delun.
units.idiomatic: On jichou Weibo troops rebelled and seized He Delun.

units.zh: 是時，朝廷既分魏博六州為兩鎮，命劉鄩統大軍屯於南樂，以討王熔為名，遣澶州刺史、行營先鋒步軍都指揮使王彥章領龍驤五百騎先入於魏州，屯於金波亭。
units.literal: The court had divided Weibo's six prefectures into two commands, ordered Liu Yan to lead the great army at Nanle in the name of attacking Wang Rong, and sent Cizhou Military Commissioner and campaign vanguard foot commander Wang Yanzhang with five hundred Dragon-Prancing cavalry into Weizhou first, encamped at Jinbo Pavilion.
units.idiomatic: The court had split Weibo, sent Liu Yan to Nanle ostensibly against Wang Rong, and Wang Yanzhang with five hundred Dragon-Prancing horse into Weizhou to camp at Jinbo Pavilion.

units.zh: 詔以魏州軍兵之半隸於相州，並徙其家焉。
units.literal: An edict placed half of Weizhou's troops under Xiangzhou and moved their families as well.
units.idiomatic: Half of Weizhou's soldiers were assigned to Xiangzhou and their families moved with them.

units.zh: 謝瞳，字子明，福州人。
units.literal: Xie Tong, styled Ziming, was a man of Fuzhou.
units.idiomatic: Xie Tong, who styled himself Ziming, came from Fuzhou.

units.zh: 唐咸通末舉進士，因留長安，三歲不中第。
units.literal: At the end of Tang Xiantong he sat the jinshi examination and remained in Chang'an; for three years he failed to place.
units.idiomatic: Late in Xiantong he sat the jinshi examination and stayed in Chang'an; three years passed without his name on the rolls.

units.zh: 廣明初，黃巢陷長安，遂投跡於太祖，洎居門下，未嘗一日不在左右。
units.literal: Early Guangming, Huang Chao took Chang'an; he then cast his lot with the Founder, and once under his gate never a day was absent from his side.
units.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an in the first year of Guangming, Tong entered the Founder's service and from that day was never far from his side.

units.zh: 文德元年十一月，蔡將申叢折宗權足，納款於太祖，使捍奏其事，加兼御史大夫。
units.literal: Wende year 1, eleventh month, the Cai general Shen Cong broke Zongquan's foot, submitted to the Founder; he had Han report the affair and added him concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Wende 1 the Cai general Shen Cong broke Zongquan's foot and surrendered; Han carried word of it to the Founder and received concurrent rank as Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 光化三年六月，太祖北伐鎮、定，至常山，而王钅容危懾，送款於太祖，命捍入壁門傳諭。
units.literal: Guanghua year 3, sixth month, the Founder north campaigned against Zhen and Ding, reaching Changshan; Wang Rong in peril and fear sent submission to the Founder, and ordered Han to enter the barbican gate to proclaim the message.
units.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guanghua 3 the Founder marched north against Zhen and Ding; at Changshan a terrified Wang Rong submitted, and the Founder sent Han through the barbican to announce terms.

units.zh: 時兩軍未整，守門者戈戟千匝，捍馳騎而入，竟達其命。
units.literal: At that time the two armies were not yet arrayed; gate guards with spears and halberds ringed a thousandfold; Han galloped in on horseback and at last delivered his charge.
units.idiomatic: While both armies were still unprepared, spears ringed the gate a thousand deep; Han rode straight through and carried out his orders.

units.zh: 周德威
units.literal: Zhou Dewei
units.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei

units.zh: 周德威，字鎮遠，朔州馬邑人也。
units.literal: Zhou Dewei, styled Zhenyuan, was a native of Mayi in Shuozhou.
units.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei, styled Zhenyuan, came from Mayi in Shuozhou.

units.zh: 為人勇而多智，能望塵以知敵數。
units.literal: As a man he was brave and full of stratagem, able to tell an enemy’s numbers from the dust they raised.
units.idiomatic: Brave and cunning, he could read an enemy’s strength from the dust on the horizon.

units.zh: 乃休士卒，遣裨將王建及牧馬於沙苑，掞以謂晉軍且懈，乃夜遁去，存審追擊於渭河，又大敗之。
units.literal: He rested the troops and sent the deputy Wang Jianji to graze horses at Shayuan. Yan thought the Jin army was slackening and fled by night; Cunshen pursued to the Wei River and again defeated him greatly.
units.idiomatic: He rested the men and sent the deputy Wang Jianji to graze horses at Shayuan. Yan took it for slackness and bolted by night. Cunshen chased him to the Wei River and broke him again.

units.zh: 張文禮弒趙王王镕，晉遣閻寶、李嗣昭等攻之，至輒戰死，最後遣存審破之。
units.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Zhao king Wang Rong. Jin sent Yan Bao, Li Sizhao, and others against him; they died in battle one after another, until at last Cunshen was sent and broke him.
units.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli murdered the Zhao king Wang Rong. Jin sent Yan Bao, Li Sizhao, and others against him; one after another they fell in battle, until Cunshen was sent and broke him at last.

units.zh: 存審為將有機略，大小百餘戰，未嘗敗衄，與周德威齊名。
units.literal: As a commander Cunshen had tactical cunning; in more than a hundred battles large and small he never suffered defeat, and his name stood equal to Zhou Dewei’s.
units.idiomatic: Cunshen commanded with cunning. In more than a hundred fights, great and small, he never tasted defeat—and his name stood beside Zhou Dewei’s.

title.zh: 卷二百一十八 列傳第一百四十三 沙陀
title.en: Volume 218 Biographies 143: Shatuo
title.raw: 卷二百一十八 列傳第一百四十三 沙陀 Volume 218 Biographies 143: Shatuo

units.zh: 沙陀，西突厥別部處月種也。
units.literal: The Shatuo were of the Chuyue branch among the dependent tribes of the Western Turks.
units.idiomatic: The Shatuo were a branch of the Chuyue people, a dependent tribe of the Western Turks.

units.zh: 始，突厥東西部分治烏孫故地，與處月、處蜜雜居。
units.literal: At first, when the Eastern and Western Turks divided rule over the former Wusun lands, they lived intermixed with the Chuyue and Chumi.
units.idiomatic: In the beginning, as the Eastern and Western Turks partitioned the old Wusun territories, they dwelt alongside the Chuyue and Chumi peoples.

units.zh: 貞觀七年，太宗以鼓纛立利邲咄陸可汗，而族人步真觖望，謀並其弟彌射乃自立。
units.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, Taizong installed Ashina Yipiduolu as khan with the drum-and-banner ceremony; the clansman Böke was discontented and plotted to join his younger brother Mishe and declare himself ruler.
units.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 (633), Emperor Taizong invested Ashina Yipiduolu as khan in the formal drum-and-banner ceremony. A clansman named Böke, resentful of the appointment, conspired to ally with his younger brother Mishe and seize power for himself.

units.zh: 克用取雲州，以部將石善友為刺史、大同軍防禦使。
units.literal: Keyong took Yunzhou and made his officer Shi Shanyou prefect and Datong Army defense commissioner.
units.idiomatic: Keyong took Yunzhou and appointed his officer Shi Shanyou prefect and defense commissioner of the Datong Army.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王镕攻堯山，克用使李嗣勛擊之，斬級三萬，克用遂拔天長，略常山，度滹沱，燔其郛。
units.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou attacked Yaoshan; Keyong sent Li Sikuen against him and took thirty thousand heads; Keyong then took Tianchang, overran Changshan, crossed the Hutuo, and burned its outer walls.
units.idiomatic: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou attacked Yaoshan. Keyong sent Li Sikuen against him and claimed thirty thousand heads. Keyong then took Tianchang, overran Changshan, crossed the Hutuo, and burned its outer walls.

units.zh: 徇地至趙，取鼓、槁二城。
units.literal: He overran the land to Zhao and took the two cities of Gu and Gao.
units.idiomatic: He overran the country as far as Zhao and took the cities of Gu and Gao.

units.zh: 列傳第四十九
units.literal: Biography 49
units.idiomatic: Biography Forty-Nine

units.zh: 江淹任昉王僧孺
units.literal: Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, Wang Sengru
units.idiomatic: Jiang Yan, Ren Fang, and Wang Sengru

units.zh: 江淹字文通，濟陽考城人也。
units.literal: Jiang Yan, courtesy name Wentong, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
units.idiomatic: Jiang Yan, styled Wentong, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

units.zh: 後為司徒竟陵王記室參軍。
units.literal: Later he served as recorder-aide to the Minister of Education, Prince Jingling.
units.idiomatic: Later he served as recorder-aide to the Minister of Education, Prince Jingling.

units.zh: 時琅邪王融有才俊，自謂無對當時，見昉之文，怳然自失。
units.literal: At that time Wang Rong of Langya had literary talent and brilliance; he considered himself without rival in the age; when he saw Fang's writings he was suddenly lost to himself.
units.idiomatic: At that time Wang Rong of Langya had literary talent and brilliance and considered himself without rival in the age. When he saw Fang's writings he was suddenly lost to himself.

units.zh: 以父喪去官，泣血三年，杖而後起。
units.literal: On his father's death he left office; he wept blood for three years and only rose with a staff.
units.idiomatic: On his father's death he left office. He wept blood for three years and only rose with a staff.

title.zh: 卷七十三 列傳第三十三 顏延之
title.en: Volume 73 Biographies 33: Yan Yanzhi
title.raw: 卷七十三 列傳第三十三 顏延之 Volume 73 Biographies 33: Yan Yanzhi

units.zh: 顏延之字延年，琅邪臨沂人也。
units.literal: Yan Yanzhi, styled Yannian, was a man of Langya, Linyi.
units.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi, whose style was Yannian, came from Langya commandery, Linyi county.

units.zh: 曾祖含，右光祿大夫。
units.literal: His great-grandfather Han was Right Director of the Imperial Household.
units.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yan Han served as Right Director of the Imperial Household.

units.zh: 祖約，零陵太守。
units.literal: His grandfather Yue was Administrator of Lingling.
units.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan Yue was Administrator of Lingling.

units.zh: 湛深恨焉，言於彭城王義康，出為永嘉太守。
units.literal: Zhan deeply hated this and spoke to Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; he was sent out as Administrator of Yongjia.
units.idiomatic: Zhan hated this deeply and spoke to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; Yanzhi was sent out as Administrator of Yongjia.

units.zh: 延之甚怨憤，乃作五君詠以述竹林七賢，山濤、王戎以貴顯被黜，詠嵇康曰：「鸞翮有時鎩，龍性誰能馴。」
units.literal: Yanzhi was very resentful and angry, and composed Odes to the Five Lords to treat the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove; Shan Tao and Wang Rong were omitted for their noble prominence. On Ji Kang he wrote: "The phoenix pinion is sometimes clipped; who can tame a dragon's nature?"
units.idiomatic: Burning with resentment, Yanzhi wrote his Odes to the Five Lords about the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove, leaving out Shan Tao and Wang Rong as men who had risen to wealth and rank. Of Ji Kang he wrote: "A phoenix wing may be clipped in its season—who can tame a dragon's nature?"

units.zh: 詠阮籍曰：「物故可不論，塗窮能無慟。」
units.literal: On Ruan Ji: "When things are past one need not discuss them; when the road ends how can one not grieve?"
units.idiomatic: Of Ruan Ji: "When things are done with, why argue? When the road runs out, who does not mourn?"

title.zh: 卷三十九 雜傳第二十七: 王鎔 羅紹威 王處直 劉守光
title.en: Volume 39 Miscellaneous Biographies 19: Wang Rong, Luo Shaowei, Wang Chuzhi, Liu Shouguang
title.raw: 卷三十九 雜傳第二十七: 王鎔 羅紹威 王處直 劉守光 Volume 39 Miscellaneous Biographies 19: Wang Rong, Luo Shaowei, Wang Chuzhi, Liu Shouguang

units.zh: 王镕，其先回鶻阿布思之遺種，曰沒諾幹，為鎮州王武俊騎將，武俊錄以為子，遂冒姓王氏。
units.literal: Wang Rong: his ancestors were descendants of the Uyghur Abu Si, named Mo Nuogan, a cavalry officer of Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou; Wujun adopted him as a son, and he took the surname Wang.
units.idiomatic: Wang Rong traced his line to Mo Nuogan, a survivor of the Uyghur chief Abu Si. Mo Nuogan served Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou as a mounted officer; Wujun adopted him, and the family took the name Wang.

units.zh: 沒諾幹子曰末垣活，末垣活子曰升，升子曰廷湊，廷湊子曰元達，元達子曰紹鼎、紹懿，紹鼎子曰景崇。
units.literal: Mo Nuogan’s son was Mo Yuanhuo; Mo Yuanhuo’s son was Sheng; Sheng’s son was Tingcou; Tingcou’s son was Yuanda; Yuanda’s sons were Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding’s son was Jingchong.
units.idiomatic: Mo Nuogan begat Mo Yuanhuo, who begat Sheng, then Tingcou, then Yuanda. Yuanda had Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding begat Jingchong.

units.zh: 自升以上三世，常為鎮州騎將，自景崇以上四世五人，皆為成德軍節度使。
units.literal: From Sheng upward for three generations they were constantly Zhenzhou cavalry officers; from Jingchong upward for four generations five men all were military commissioners of the Chengde army.
units.idiomatic: For three generations before Sheng the family held cavalry commands at Zhenzhou; for four generations from Jingchong, five men in succession ruled Chengde.

units.zh: 乃為之班師。
units.literal: Thereupon they withdrew the army for him.
units.idiomatic: For his sake they turned back.

units.zh: 守光益以為諸鎮畏其強，乃諷諸鎮共推尊己，於是晉王率天德宋瑤、振武周德威、昭義李嗣昭、義武王處直、成德王镕等，以墨制冊尊守光為尚書令、尚父。
units.literal: Shouguang thought still more that the circuits feared his strength; he hinted that the circuits jointly exalt him. Thereupon the Prince of Jin led Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Wang Rong of Chengde, and others, with ink edicts enfeoffing Shouguang as Director-in-Chief and Imperial Father.
units.idiomatic: Shouguang took this as proof that every circuit feared him and began pressing them to elevate him together. The Prince of Jin then had Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Wang Rong of Chengde, and others issue ink edicts naming Shouguang Director-in-Chief and Imperial Father.

units.zh: 守光又遣告於梁，請授己河北兵馬都統，以討鎮、定、河東。
units.literal: Shouguang also sent word to Liang, asking to be appointed commander-in-chief of Hebei military and horse, to attack Zhen, Ding, and Hedong.
units.idiomatic: Shouguang also petitioned Liang to make him overall commander of Hebei armies and cavalry, with orders to strike Zhen, Ding, and Hedong.

units.zh: 守光叩頭請死，命械守光並其父仁恭以從軍。
units.literal: Shouguang kowtowed begging death. He ordered Shouguang fettered together with his father Rengong to follow the army.
units.idiomatic: Shouguang kowtowed and begged for death. The Prince had him shackled to his father Rengong and marched them with the army.

units.zh: 軍還過趙，趙王王镕會晉王，置酒，酒酣請曰：「願見仁恭父子。」
units.literal: The army returned passing through Zhao. Zhao king Wang Rong met the Prince of Jin and set out wine. When the wine was heated he requested: “I would see father and son Rengong.”
units.idiomatic: On the march home through Zhao, Wang Rong entertained the Prince of Jin. When the cups were warm he asked: “Let me see Rengong and his son.”

units.zh: 晉王命破械出之，引置下坐。
units.literal: The Prince ordered their fetters broken and them brought out, seated below him.
units.idiomatic: The Prince had their bonds removed and them brought out to sit below the dais.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.literal: Alas!
units.idiomatic: Alas!

units.zh: 孟子謂「春秋無義戰」，予亦以謂五代無全臣。
units.literal: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I likewise hold that in the Five Dynasties there were no whole ministers.
units.idiomatic: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I say the Five Dynasties knew no ministers whole in loyalty.

units.zh: 無者，非無一人，蓋僅有之耳，余得死節之士三人焉。
units.literal: “None” does not mean not a single man—it means barely any; I found three men who died for principle.
units.idiomatic: “None” is not literally none—only a handful; I count three who died for principle.

units.zh: 是時，守文亦求救於晉，晉為攻邢、洺以牽之，從周遽還，敗晉兵於青山。
units.literal: At this time Shouwen also begged Jin for help; Jin attacked Xing and Ming to draw Congzhou off. Congzhou hurried back and defeated Jin troops at Qingshan.
units.idiomatic: Shouwen also called on Jin, which struck Xing and Ming to pull Congzhou away. Congzhou turned back and beat the Jin at Qingshan.

units.zh: 遂從太祖攻鎮州，下臨城，王熔乞盟，太祖表從周泰寧軍節度使。
units.literal: Then he followed Taizu against Zhenzhou, took Lincheng. Wang Rong asked for peace; Taizu memorialized to make Congzhou military governor of Taining.
units.idiomatic: He followed Taizu against Zhenzhou and took Lincheng. Wang Rong sued for peace; Taizu made Congzhou military governor of Taining.

units.zh: 從氏叔琮攻晉太原，不克。
units.literal: Congzhou joined Shi Shuzong in attacking Taiyuan of Jin but could not take it.
units.idiomatic: Congzhou joined Shi Shuzong against Taiyuan but could not take it.

units.literal: Alas!
units.idiomatic: Alas!

units.zh: 孟子謂「春秋無義戰」，予亦以謂五代無全臣。
units.literal: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I likewise hold that in the Five Dynasties there were no whole ministers.
units.idiomatic: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I say the Five Dynasties knew no ministers whole in loyalty.

units.zh: 無者，非無一人，蓋僅有之耳，余得死節之士三人焉。
units.literal: “None” does not mean not a single man—it means barely any; I found three men who died for principle.
units.idiomatic: “None” is not literally none—only a handful; I count three who died for principle.

units.zh: 太祖初鎮宣武，以為客將，使從朱珍募兵淄青。
units.literal: When Taizu first took command of Xuanwu, he made Han a guest officer and had him follow Zhu Zhen to recruit troops in Ziqing.
units.idiomatic: When Taizu first secured Xuanwu, he made Han a guest officer and sent him with Zhu Zhen to raise troops in Ziqing.

units.zh: 太祖北攻鎮州，與王鎔和，遣捍見鎔，鎔軍未知梁意，方嚴兵，捍馳一騎入城中，諭鎔以太祖意，鎔乃聽命。
units.literal: When Taizu marched north against Zhenzhou and made peace with Wang Rong, he sent Han to see Rong. Rong’s army did not yet know Liang’s intent and stood in strict readiness; Han galloped alone into the city, explained Taizu’s purpose to Rong, and Rong then obeyed.
units.idiomatic: When Taizu marched north on Zhenzhou and made peace with Wang Rong, he sent Han to see him. Rong’s army did not know Liang’s intent and stood on alert; Han rode alone into the city, explained Taizu’s purpose, and Rong submitted.

units.zh: 梁兵攻定州，降王處直，捍復以一騎入慰城中。
units.literal: When Liang troops attacked Dingzhou and Wang Chuzhi submitted, Han again entered the city alone on horseback to reassure the people within.
units.idiomatic: When Liang took Dingzhou and Wang Chuzhi submitted, Han again rode in alone to reassure the city.

units.literal: Biographies, number fifty.
units.idiomatic: the 50th year of Biographies

units.literal: Fan Xia, Fu Zhao, Kong Xiuyuan, Jiang Ge, Xu Mian, Xu Mao, Yin Jun.
units.idiomatic: Fan Xia, Fu Zhao, Kong Xiuyuan, Jiang Ge, Xu Mian, Xu Mao, and Yin Jun

units.zh: 高祖宣，晉徵士。
units.literal: His great-great-grandfather Xuan was a summoned scholar under Jin.
units.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Xuan had been a summoned scholar under Jin.

units.zh: 觀此足稱王佐之才。」
units.literal: Judging from this, he fully deserves to be called talent for assisting a king."
units.idiomatic: From this one can see that he truly possesses the talent of a chief minister."

units.zh: 琅邪王融雅相友善，乃薦之于司徒竟陵王，為西邸學士。
units.literal: Wang Rong of Langya was elegantly friendly with him and recommended him to Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, as a scholar of the Western Lodge.
units.idiomatic: Wang Rong of Langya became his close friend and recommended him to Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, who appointed him a scholar of the Western Lodge.

units.zh: 梁台建，與南陽劉之遴同為太學博士，當時以為美選。
units.literal: When the Liang administration was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang both served as erudites of the Imperial University; at the time this was considered a fine selection.
units.idiomatic: When the Liang administration was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang were both appointed erudites of the Imperial University, a pairing widely regarded as an excellent choice.

title.en: Volume 77 Biographies 67: Noble Favorites
title.raw: 卷七十七 列傳第六十七 恩倖 Volume 77 Biographies 67: Noble Favorites

units.zh: 戴法興 徐爰 阮佃夫 紀僧真 劉系宗 茹法亮 呂文顯 茹法珍 周石珍 陸驗 司馬申 施文慶 沈客卿 孔範
units.literal: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan
units.idiomatic: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan

units.zh: 夫鮑魚芳蘭，在於所習，中人之性，可以上下。
units.literal: Now salted fish and fragrant orchids alike depend on what one is accustomed to; the nature of an average person may be raised or lowered.
units.idiomatic: Just as salted fish and orchids take their character from their surroundings, so too can an ordinary person's nature be elevated or debased by habit.

units.zh: 然則謀于管仲，齊桓有邵陵之師，邇于易牙，小白掩陽門之扇。
units.literal: Thus when he took counsel with Guan Zhong, Duke Huan of Qi had armies at Shaoling; when he drew close to Yi Ya, Duke Huan was shut behind the Yang Gate.
units.idiomatic: When Duke Huan of Qi listened to Guan Zhong, he led armies as far as Shaoling; when he grew intimate with Yi Ya, he ended shut in behind the Yang Gate.

units.zh: 又自陳曰：「珍之西州伏事，侍從入宮，契闊心膂，竭盡誠力。
units.literal: He also declared in his own person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.
units.idiomatic: He also declared in person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed the emperor into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.

units.zh: 王融奸謀潛構，自非珍之翼衛扶持，事在不測。
units.literal: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery; had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.
units.idiomatic: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery. Had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.

units.zh: 今惜千戶侯，誰為官使者。」
units.literal: Now if you begrudge me a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?"
units.idiomatic: If you begrudge me now a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?"

units.zh: 劉福，徐州下邳人。
units.literal: Liu Fu was a native of Xiapi in Xuzhou.
units.idiomatic: Liu Fu was from Xiapi in Xuzhou.

units.zh: 少倜儻，魁岸有膂力。
units.literal: In youth he was unrestrained and free-spirited, with a towering frame and great physical strength.
units.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and unconventional, tall and powerfully built.

units.zh: 周顯德中，世宗征淮南，福徒步謁見於壽春。
units.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, when the Shizong Emperor campaigned against Huainan, Fu went on foot to present himself at Shouchun.
units.idiomatic: During the Xiande reign of the Later Zhou, when Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, Fu walked to Shouchun to seek an audience.

units.zh: 明年，拜殿前都虞候，領容州觀察使。
units.literal: The next year he was appointed chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and concurrently observation commissioner of Rongzhou.
units.idiomatic: The following year he was made chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and concurrently observation commissioner of Rongzhou.

units.zh: 一日，侍宴北苑，上入玄武門，守正大醉，與王榮論邊功於駕前，忿爭失儀，侍臣請以屬吏，上弗許。
units.literal: One day, while attending a feast in the Northern Park, as the emperor entered the Xuanwu Gate, Shouzheng was greatly drunk and with Wang Rong disputed frontier merit before the imperial carriage, quarreling in anger and losing propriety; attendants asked that they be handed to the judicial officers, but the emperor would not permit it.
units.idiomatic: One day at a feast in the Northern Park, as the emperor passed through the Xuanwu Gate, Shouzheng, very drunk, argued with Wang Rong over frontier exploits before the imperial carriage, quarreling loudly and forgetting decorum; attendants asked that they be turned over to the judicial authorities, but the emperor refused.

units.zh: 翌日，俱詣殿廷請罪，上曰：「朕亦大醉，漫不復省。」
units.literal: The next day they both came to the palace hall to plead guilty; the emperor said, "I too was greatly drunk and scarcely remember it."
units.idiomatic: The next day both came to court to apologize; the emperor said, "I was drunk myself and scarcely remember it."

units.zh: 丁會，字道隱，壽州壽春人。
units.literal: Ding Hui, style name Daoyin, was a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.
units.idiomatic: Ding Hui, whose style name was Daoyin, came from Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.

units.zh: 父季。
units.literal: His father was Ji.
units.idiomatic: His father was named Ji.

units.zh: 會幼放蕩縱橫，不治農產，恒隨哀挽者學紼謳，尤嗜其聲。
units.literal: As a youth Hui was wild and unrestrained, did not tend the family farms, always followed funeral mourners to learn pall-rope dirges, and was especially fond of their sound.
units.idiomatic: In youth Ding Hui was unruly and idle, neglected the family fields, and constantly trailed funeral parties to learn mourning dirges for the pall ropes; he loved their cadence above all else.

units.zh: 弱冠從軍，初為鎮州隊長，以功漸升部將，與符習從征於河上，頗得士心。
units.literal: At weak cap he entered the army, at first was squad leader of Zhen Prefecture, through merit gradually rose to section commander, followed Fu Xi in campaigns along the river, and greatly won the soldiers' hearts.
units.idiomatic: At twenty he entered the army as a squad leader in Zhenzhou, rose by merit to section commander, marched with Fu Xi on the Yellow River campaigns, and won strong loyalty from his men.

units.zh: 聞張文禮弑王鎔，誌復主讎，雪泣請行。
units.literal: When he heard Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong, he resolved to avenge his lord, wept tears of grief, and requested to march.
units.idiomatic: When he heard that Zhang Wenli had murdered Wang Rong, he vowed to avenge his lord, wept aloud, and begged to march.

units.zh: 兵及恒陽，文禮執其母妻洎兒女十口誘之，不回，攻城日急。
units.literal: When the army reached Hengyang, Wenli seized his mother, wife, and together with sons and daughters ten mouths to entice him, but he did not turn back; the siege of the city grew daily more urgent.
units.idiomatic: When the army reached Hengyang, Wenli seized his mother, wife, and children—ten persons in all—to lure him back, but he would not turn aside, and the siege pressed harder day by day.

units.zh: 二王諸葛李孟
units.literal: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng
units.idiomatic: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng

units.zh: 王重榮，太原祁人。
units.literal: Wang Chongrong was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
units.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 父縱，太和末為河中騎將，從石雄破回鶻，終鹽州刺史。
units.literal: His father Zong, at the end of the Taihe era served as a cavalry officer in Hezhong, followed Shi Xiong in defeating the Uyghurs, and ended as governor of Yanzhou.
units.idiomatic: His father Zong, in the closing years of the Taihe reign, served as a cavalry officer in Hezhong; he followed Shi Xiong against the Uyghurs and eventually became governor of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 而全忠以克用方強，不敢加兵。
units.literal: But Quanzhong, because Keyong was then strong, did not dare send troops against him.
units.idiomatic: Quanzhong, however, dared not attack while Keyong was still strong.

units.zh: 及王镕詘服，拔定州，而克用兵折，乃謂其將張存敬曰：「珂恃太原侮慢我，爾持一繩縛之。」
units.literal: When Wang Rong submitted and Ding Prefecture was taken, and Keyong's military strength was broken, he then said to his general Zhang Cunjing, "Ke relies on Taiyuan and insults me—take a rope and bind him."
units.idiomatic: When Wang Rong submitted and Ding Prefecture fell, and Keyong's armies were spent, he told his general Zhang Cunjing, "Ke leans on Taiyuan and insults me—take a rope and bind him."

units.zh: 存敬以兵數萬度河，由含山襲，絳州刺史陶建釗、晉州刺史張漢瑜皆降，以何絪戍之，進攻珂。
units.literal: Cunjing led tens of thousands of troops across the river, struck by way of Hanshan, and the governors of Jiang and Jin, Tao Jianzhao and Zhang Hanyu, both surrendered. He garrisoned the territory with He Yin and advanced to attack Ke.
units.idiomatic: Cunjing crossed the river with tens of thousands of men and struck through Hanshan. The governors of Jiang and Jin, Tao Jianzhao and Zhang Hanyu, both surrendered. He left He Yin to garrison the region and marched against Ke.

title.zh: 卷二十一 列傳第十一 王弘
title.en: Volume 21 Biographies 11: Wang Hong
title.raw: 卷二十一 列傳第十一 王弘 Volume 21 Biographies 11: Wang Hong

units.zh: 王弘，字休元，琅邪临沂人也。
units.literal: Wang Hong, styled Xiuyuan, was a man of Langya Linyi.
units.idiomatic: Wang Hong, courtesy name Xiuyuan, came from Langya commandery, Linyi county.

units.zh: 曾祖导，晋丞相，祖洽，中领军，父珣，司徒。
units.literal: His great-grandfather Dao was Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia was Central Army Commander; his father Xun was Minister of Education.
units.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dao had served as Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia as Central Army Commander; his father Xun as Minister of Education.

units.zh: 弘少好學，以清悟知名。
units.literal: Hong from youth loved learning and was famed for lucid insight.
units.idiomatic: From boyhood Hong loved study and won renown for clear, penetrating mind.

units.zh: 元徽中，為廬陵內史，未至郡，卒。
units.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was Interior Minister of Luling; before reaching the commandery he died.
units.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era he was appointed Interior Minister of Luling but died before reaching his post.

units.zh: 僧達孫 融
units.literal: Sengda's grandson Rong
units.idiomatic: Sengda's grandson Rong

units.zh: 融字元長，少而神明警慧。
units.literal: Rong, styled Yuanchang, from youth was bright and keenly intelligent.
units.idiomatic: Rong, courtesy name Yuanchang, was bright and precocious from childhood.

units.zh: 母臨川太守謝惠宣女，性敦敏，教融書學。
units.literal: His mother was daughter of Xie Huixuan, Administrator of Linchuan; she was earnest and quick, and taught Rong letters and learning.
units.idiomatic: His mother was a daughter of Xie Huixuan, Administrator of Linchuan; earnest and quick herself, she taught Rong reading and scholarship.

units.zh: 博涉有文才，從叔儉謂人曰：「此兒至四十，名位自然及祖。」
units.literal: Broadly read and possessed of literary talent, his father's younger cousin Jian told others: "This boy at forty will naturally reach his grandfather's name and rank."
units.idiomatic: Well read and gifted in letters, his father's younger cousin Jian told others: "At forty this boy will naturally match his grandfather in rank and fame."

units.zh: 舉秀才，累遷太子舍人。
units.literal: He was recommended as Presented Scholar and was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
units.idiomatic: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he rose to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 以父宦不通，弱年便欲紹興家業，啟齊武帝求自試，遷秘書丞。
units.literal: Because his father's official career had not prospered, in weak years he wished to revive the family estate; he memorialized Emperor Wu of Qi asking to prove himself and was transferred to Secretary.
units.idiomatic: His father's career had stalled; while still young Rong sought to revive the family fortunes, petitioned Emperor Wu of Qi for a trial appointment, and was made Secretary.

units.zh: 從叔儉初有儀同之授，贈儉詩及書，儉甚奇之，笑謂人曰：「穰侯印詎便可解。」
units.literal: When his father's younger cousin Jian first received appointment as Equal to the Three Excellencies, Rong sent him a poem and letter; Jian marveled greatly and smiling told others: "Can the seal of Ranghou really be taken off so soon?"
units.idiomatic: When his cousin Jian first received appointment as Equal to the Three Excellencies, Rong sent him a poem and letter; Jian was astonished and smiled: "So the seal of Ranghou can be handed over already?"

units.zh: 曆丹陽丞，中書郎。
units.literal: He served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
units.idiomatic: He served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Gentleman of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 永明末，武帝欲北侵，使毛惠秀畫漢武北伐圖，融因此上疏，開張北侵之議。
units.literal: At the end of the Yongming era Emperor Wu wished to invade the north and had Mao Huixiu paint Emperor Wu of Han's northern campaign; Rong therefore submitted a memorial opening discussion of northern invasion.
units.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming, when Emperor Wu planned a northern campaign and had Mao Huixiu paint Han Wudi's northern expedition, Rong submitted a memorial urging invasion.

units.zh: 圖成，上置琅邪城射堂壁上，遊幸輒觀焉。
units.literal: When the painting was finished the emperor placed it on the wall of the archery hall at Langya city and viewed it whenever he toured.
units.idiomatic: When the painting was finished the emperor hung it in the archery hall at Langya city and viewed it on every visit.

units.zh: 九年，芳林園禊宴，使融為曲水詩序，當時稱之。
units.literal: In the ninth year, at the Fanglin Garden spring purification feast, he had Rong compose the preface to the winding-water poems; men of the time praised it.
units.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at the Fanglin Garden spring purification, he had Rong write the preface to the winding-water poems; contemporaries praised it.

units.zh: 上以融才辯，使兼主客，接魏使房景高、宋弁。
units.literal: The emperor, because Rong was talented and eloquent, had him additionally serve as Chief of Guests and receive the Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.
units.idiomatic: The emperor, noting Rong's eloquence, also made him Chief of Guests to receive the Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.

units.zh: 弁見融年少，問：「主客年幾？」
units.literal: Bian saw Rong was young and asked: "How old is the Chief of Guests?"
units.idiomatic: Bian saw that Rong was young and asked: "How old is the Chief of Guests?"

units.zh: 融曰：「五十之年，久踰其半。」
units.literal: Rong said: "Of fifty years, long past the half."
units.idiomatic: Rong replied: "Fifty years—well past the halfway mark."

units.zh: 景高又云：「在北聞主客曲水詩序勝延年，實願一見。」
units.literal: Jinggao also said: "In the north I heard the Chief of Guests' preface to the winding-water poems surpasses Yannian; I truly wish to see it."
units.idiomatic: Jinggao added: "In the north I heard your winding-water preface surpasses Yannian's—I long to see it."

units.zh: 融乃示之。
units.literal: Rong then showed it.
units.idiomatic: Rong showed it to them.

units.zh: 後日，宋弁於瑤池堂謂融曰：「昔觀相如封禪，以知漢武之德，今覽王生詩序，用見齊主之盛。」
units.literal: Later, Song Bian at Yaochi Hall said to Rong: "Once reading Sima Xiangru's feng and shan text, one knew the virtue of Han Wu; now reading Master Wang's poem preface, one sees the splendor of the Qi lord."
units.idiomatic: Later at Yaochi Hall Song Bian told Rong: "Reading Sima Xiangru's feng-shan text revealed Han Wudi's virtue; reading Master Wang's preface reveals our lord's splendor."

units.zh: 融曰：「皇家盛明，豈直比蹤漢武，更慚鄙制，無以遠匹相如。」
units.literal: Rong said: "Our house's brilliance—how could it merely follow Han Wu? I am all the more ashamed of my crude composition; it cannot remotely match Xiangru."
units.idiomatic: Rong replied: "Our dynasty's brilliance far exceeds Han Wudi's; my humble piece cannot compare with Xiangru."

units.zh: 上以魏所送馬不稱，使融問之曰：「秦西冀北，實多駿驥，而魏之良馬，乃駑不若，將旦旦信誓，有時而爽，駉駉之牧，遂不能嗣？」
units.literal: The emperor, because the horses Wei sent were unworthy, had Rong ask: "West of Qin and north of Ji truly have many fine steeds, yet Wei's good horses are inferior nags—is the daily sworn faith sometimes broken, and the pastures of spirited horses no longer bred?"
units.idiomatic: Because the horses Wei sent were poor, the emperor had Rong ask: "Qin west and Ji north abound in fine steeds, yet Wei's gifts are nags—has sworn faith broken, and the pastures failed?"

units.zh: 宋弁曰：「當是不習地土。」
units.literal: Song Bian said: "Perhaps they are unused to the soil."
units.idiomatic: Song Bian said: "Perhaps they are unused to the soil here."

units.zh: 融曰：「周穆馬跡遍於天下，若騏騮之性，因地而遷，則造父之策，有時而躓。」
units.literal: Rong said: "King Mu of Zhou's horses' tracks covered the world; if the nature of qiji and juli shifts with land, then Zaofu's methods would sometimes stumble."
units.idiomatic: Rong said: "King Mu's horses ranged the world; if fine breeds change with soil, then Zaofu's art would sometimes fail."

units.zh: 弁曰：「王主客何為勤勤於千里？」
units.literal: Bian said: "Why is the Chief of Guests so earnest about a thousand li?"
units.idiomatic: Bian asked: "Why is the Chief of Guests so eager for horses from a thousand li away?"

units.zh: 融曰：「卿國既異其優劣，聊復相訪，若千里斯至，聖上當駕鼓車。」
units.literal: Rong said: "Since your state differs on quality, I merely inquire again; if they arrive from a thousand li, the sage emperor will drive the drum carriage."
units.idiomatic: Rong said: "Since your state disputes their quality, I ask again—if they truly come from afar, our emperor will drive the drum carriage to meet them."

units.zh: 弁曰：「向意既須，必不能駕鼓車也。」
units.literal: Bian said: "Since the intent is need, they surely cannot drive the drum carriage."
units.idiomatic: Bian said: "If you truly need them, you surely will not send the drum carriage."

units.zh: 融曰：「買死馬之骨，亦以郭隗之故。」
units.literal: Rong said: "Buying the bones of dead horses is also for Guo Kui's sake."
units.idiomatic: Rong said: "Even buying dead horses' bones honors Guo Kui's memory."

units.zh: 弁不能答。
units.literal: Bian could not answer.
units.idiomatic: Bian had no reply.

units.zh: 融躁于名利，自恃人地，三十內望為公輔。
units.literal: Rong was impatient for fame and profit; relying on his birth and station, before thirty he looked to become chief minister and assistant.
units.idiomatic: Rong hungered for fame and office; trusting in birth and rank, before thirty he expected the highest posts.

units.zh: 初為司徒法曹，詣王僧佑，因遇沈昭略，未相識。
units.literal: At first as Law Clerk of the Minister of Education he called on Wang Sengyou and chanced to meet Shen Zhaolüe, whom he did not know.
units.idiomatic: Early in his career, as Law Clerk of the Minister of Education, he called on Wang Sengyou and met Shen Zhaolüe, a stranger to him.

units.zh: 昭略屢顧盼，謂主人曰：「是何年少？」
units.literal: Zhaolüe looked back repeatedly and said to the host: "What youth is this?"
units.idiomatic: Zhaolüe glanced back again and again and asked the host: "Who is this young man?"

units.zh: 融殊不平，謂曰：「僕出於扶桑，入于湯穀，照耀天下，誰雲不知，而卿此問？」
units.literal: Rong was greatly displeased and said: "I come from Fusang and enter Tanggu, shining on all under heaven—who says they do not know, yet you ask this?"
units.idiomatic: Rong was furious: "I rise from Fusang and set in Tanggu, shining over the world—who does not know me, that you should ask?"

units.zh: 昭略云：「不知許事，且食蛤蜊。」
units.literal: Zhaolüe said: "I know nothing of such things—let us eat clams."
units.idiomatic: Zhaolüe said: "I know nothing of that—let us eat clams instead."

units.zh: 融曰：「物以群分，方以類聚，君長東隅，居然應嗜此族。」
units.literal: Rong said: "Things group by kind, regions by class—you preside over the eastern corner and naturally should love this tribe."
units.idiomatic: Rong retorted: "Things flock by kind and regions by class—you rule the eastern corner and naturally favor this tribe."

units.zh: 其高自標置如此。
units.literal: Such was his lofty self-regard.
units.idiomatic: Such was his towering self-regard.

title.zh: 卷三十九 雜傳第二十七: 王鎔 羅紹威 王處直 劉守光
title.en: Volume 39 Miscellaneous Biographies 19: Wang Rong, Luo Shaowei, Wang Chuzhi, Liu Shouguang
title.raw: 卷三十九 雜傳第二十七: 王鎔 羅紹威 王處直 劉守光 Volume 39 Miscellaneous Biographies 19: Wang Rong, Luo Shaowei, Wang Chuzhi, Liu Shouguang

units.zh: 王镕，其先回鶻阿布思之遺種，曰沒諾幹，為鎮州王武俊騎將，武俊錄以為子，遂冒姓王氏。
units.literal: Wang Rong: his ancestors were descendants of the Uyghur Abu Si, named Mo Nuogan, a cavalry officer of Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou; Wujun adopted him as a son, and he took the surname Wang.
units.idiomatic: Wang Rong traced his line to Mo Nuogan, a survivor of the Uyghur chief Abu Si. Mo Nuogan served Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou as a mounted officer; Wujun adopted him, and the family took the name Wang.

units.zh: 沒諾幹子曰末垣活，末垣活子曰升，升子曰廷湊，廷湊子曰元達，元達子曰紹鼎、紹懿，紹鼎子曰景崇。
units.literal: Mo Nuogan’s son was Mo Yuanhuo; Mo Yuanhuo’s son was Sheng; Sheng’s son was Tingcou; Tingcou’s son was Yuanda; Yuanda’s sons were Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding’s son was Jingchong.
units.idiomatic: Mo Nuogan begat Mo Yuanhuo, who begat Sheng, then Tingcou, then Yuanda. Yuanda had Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding begat Jingchong.

units.zh: 自升以上三世，常為鎮州騎將，自景崇以上四世五人，皆為成德軍節度使。
units.literal: From Sheng upward for three generations they were constantly Zhenzhou cavalry officers; from Jingchong upward for four generations five men all were military commissioners of the Chengde army.
units.idiomatic: For three generations before Sheng the family held cavalry commands at Zhenzhou; for four generations from Jingchong, five men in succession ruled Chengde.

units.zh: 太祖即位，封處直北平王。
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne he enfeoffed Chuzhi Prince of Beiping.
units.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne he made Chuzhi Prince of Beiping.

units.zh: 其後梁兵攻王鎔，鎔求救于晉，處直亦遣人至晉，願絕梁以自効。
units.literal: Later when Liang attacked Wang Rong and Rong begged Jin for aid, Chuzhi too sent envoys to Jin offering to break with Liang and prove his worth.
units.idiomatic: Later, when Liang attacked Wang Rong and Rong called on Jin, Chuzhi also sent envoys offering to break with Liang and prove his loyalty.

units.zh: 晉兵救鎔，處直以兵五千從，破梁軍於柏鄉。
units.literal: Jin marched to save Rong; Chuzhi followed with five thousand men and defeated Liang at Baixiang.
units.idiomatic: Jin marched to save Rong; Chuzhi brought five thousand men and helped break Liang at Baixiang.

units.zh: 其後晉北破燕，南取魏博，與梁戰河上，十餘年，處直未嘗不以兵從。
units.literal: Thereafter Jin broke Yan in the north and took Weibo in the south and fought Liang along the Yellow River for more than ten years; Chuzhi never failed to follow with troops.
units.idiomatic: For more than ten years Jin broke Yan in the north, seized Weibo in the south, and fought Liang along the river; Chuzhi always marched with them.

units.zh: 都為人狡佞多謀，處直以為節度副使。
units.literal: Du was crafty, fawning, and full of schemes; Chuzhi made him deputy military commissioner.
units.idiomatic: Du was sly, flattering, and scheming. Chuzhi made him deputy commissioner.

units.zh: 張文禮弒王镕，莊宗發兵討文禮，處直與左右謀曰：「鎮，定之蔽也，文禮雖有罪，然鎮亡定不獨存。」
units.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong; Zhuangzong raised troops to punish Wenli. Chuzhi consulted his close advisers, saying: “Zhen and Ding shield each other; though Wenli is guilty, if Zhen perishes Ding cannot stand alone.”
units.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong, and Zhuangzong marched to punish him. Chuzhi told his intimates: “Zhen and Ding are one shield. Wenli may be guilty, but if Zhen falls, Ding cannot stand alone.”

units.zh: 乃遣人請莊宗毋發兵，莊宗取所獲文禮與梁蠟書示處直曰：「文禮負我，師不可止。」
units.literal: He sent men to ask Zhuangzong not to march; Zhuangzong took the captured letters between Wenli and Liang sealed in wax and showed Chuzhi, saying: “Wenli has betrayed me—the army cannot stop.”
units.idiomatic: He sent envoys begging Zhuangzong to stay his hand. Zhuangzong showed him the wax-sealed letters Wenli had sent Liang: “Wenli has betrayed me. The campaign does not stop.”

units.zh: 朱宣
units.literal: Zhu Xuan
units.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan

units.literal: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉
units.idiomatic: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉

units.zh: 朱宣，宋州下邑人也。
units.literal: Zhu Xuan was a native of Xiayi in Song prefecture.
units.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan came from Xiayi in Songzhou.

units.zh: 方立以孤城自守，求救于梁，梁方東事兗、鄆，不能救也。
units.literal: Fangli held his lone city and begged Liang for help, but Liang was then engaged in the east at Yan and Yun and could not save him.
units.idiomatic: Fangli held out in his lone city and begged Liang for help, but Liang was tied down in Yan and Yun and could not come.

units.zh: 文德元年，方立乞兵于王鎔以攻晉，鎔許之。
units.literal: In the first year of Wende, Fangli asked Wang Rong for troops to attack Jin; Rong agreed.
units.idiomatic: In Wende 1 Fangli asked Wang Rong for troops against Jin; Rong agreed.

units.zh: 方立乃遣其將奚忠信攻晉遼州，而鎔以佗故不能出兵。
units.literal: Fangli sent his general Xi Zhongxin to attack Jin’s Liaozhou, but Rong for other reasons could not march.
units.idiomatic: Fangli sent Xi Zhongxin against Jin’s Liaozhou, but Rong could not march for other reasons.

units.zh: 兵既失約，忠信大敗，而晉兵乘勝攻之。
units.literal: When the promised troops failed to come, Zhongxin was utterly defeated, and Jin forces pressed the attack.
units.idiomatic: When the promised troops never came, Zhongxin was smashed and Jin pressed the attack.

title.raw: 卷五十九 唐書35: 列傳11 丁會 閻寶 符習 烏震 王瓚 袁象先 張溫 李紹文 Volume 59 Book of Later Tang 35: Biographies 11: Ding Hui, Yan Bao, Fu Xi, Wu Zhen, Wang Zan, Yuan Xiangxian, Zhang Wen, Li Shaowen

units.zh: 丁會，字道隱，壽州壽春人。
units.literal: Ding Hui, style name Daoyin, was a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.
units.idiomatic: Ding Hui, whose style name was Daoyin, came from Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.

units.zh: 父季。
units.literal: His father was Ji.
units.idiomatic: His father was named Ji.

units.zh: 會幼放蕩縱橫，不治農產，恒隨哀挽者學紼謳，尤嗜其聲。
units.literal: As a youth Hui was wild and unrestrained, did not tend the family farms, always followed funeral mourners to learn pall-rope dirges, and was especially fond of their sound.
units.idiomatic: In youth Ding Hui was unruly and idle, neglected the family fields, and constantly trailed funeral parties to learn mourning dirges for the pall ropes; he loved their cadence above all else.

units.zh: 符習，趙州昭慶縣人。
units.literal: Fu Xi, a native of Zhaoqing County in Zhao Prefecture.
units.idiomatic: Fu Xi came from Zhaoqing County in Zhao Prefecture.

units.zh: 少從軍，事節度使王鎔，積功至列校。
units.literal: In youth he entered the army, served Military Commissioner Wang Rong, and through accumulated merit rose to regimental commander.
units.idiomatic: He entered the army young, served the Zhao military commissioner Wang Rong, and by steady merit rose to regimental commander.

units.zh: 自莊宗經略河朔，與鎔連衡，常令習率師從莊宗征討。
units.literal: From when Zhuangzong planned the Hebei north and allied with Rong, he constantly ordered Xi to lead troops following Zhuangzong in campaigns.
units.idiomatic: Once Zhuangzong began his campaigns in the Hebei north and allied with Wang Rong, he regularly ordered Fu Xi to lead Zhao troops on Zhuangzong's campaigns.

units.zh: 鎔為張文禮所害，時習在德勝寨，文禮上書請習等歸鎮。
units.literal: When Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli, at the time Xi was at Desheng Stockade; Wenli sent a letter requesting Xi and others return to the commandery.
units.idiomatic: When Wang Rong was murdered by Zhang Wenli, Fu Xi was at Desheng Stockade. Wenli wrote asking Xi and his officers to return to Zhao.

units.zh: 習雨泣訴於莊宗曰：「臣本趙人，家世事王氏，故使嘗授臣一劍，俾臣平蕩凶寇。
units.literal: Xi wept in the rain and appealed to Zhuangzong, saying: "Your subject is originally a man of Zhao; for generations my family served the Wang house. The late lord once bestowed on your subject one sword, ordering your subject to pacify and sweep away the fierce bandits.
units.idiomatic: Fu Xi wept bitterly before Zhuangzong and said, "I am a man of Zhao. For generations my house served the Wang family. The late lord once gave me a sword and charged me to crush the murderers.

units.zh: 自聞變故，徒懷冤憤，欲以自剄，無益於營魂。
units.literal: Since hearing of the calamity I have only harbored grievance and rage, wishing to cut my own throat, which would be of no benefit to the late lord's spirit.
units.idiomatic: Since I heard what befell him I have lived only with outrage. I might cut my own throat, but that would do my dead lord's spirit no good.

units.zh: 且張文禮乃幽、滄叛將，趙王知人不盡，過意任使，致被反噬。
units.literal: Moreover Zhang Wenli is a rebel general of You and Cang; the Prince of Zhao did not fully know men, excessively trusted and employed him, and thus was bitten in return.
units.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli was a turncoat from You and Cang. The Prince of Zhao misjudged him, trusted him too far, and was destroyed for it.

units.zh: 臣雖不武，願在霸府血戰而死，不能委身於凶首。」
units.literal: Though your subject is not martial, I wish to die fighting bloodily in the hegemon's court and cannot entrust my person to the murderous chief."
units.idiomatic: I am no great warrior, but I would rather die fighting in your service than submit to that murderer."

units.zh: 吾當助爾。」
units.literal: I shall assist you."
units.idiomatic: I will help you do it."

units.zh: 習等舉身投地，號慟感激，謝曰：「王必以故使輔翼之勞，雪其冤恥，臣不敢期師旅為助，但悉本軍可以誅其逆豎。」
units.literal: Xi and the others threw their bodies to the ground, wailed in grief with gratitude, and thanked him, saying: "Your Majesty will surely, because of the late lord's labor in assisting, wipe away his grievance and shame; your subject does not dare expect army support, only that the entire native army can execute the rebellious villain."
units.idiomatic: Fu Xi and his officers prostrated themselves, wept in gratitude, and said, "If Your Majesty will honor our late lord's service and avenge his death, I do not ask for a great host—only let my own Zhao troops strike down the traitor."

units.zh: 莊宗即令閻寶、史建瑭助習討文禮，乃以習為成德軍兵馬留後。
units.literal: Zhuangzong immediately ordered Yan Bao and Shi Jiantang to assist Xi in attacking Wenli, and made Xi acting military governor of the Chengde army.
units.idiomatic: Zhuangzong at once ordered Yan Bao and Shi Jiantang to aid Fu Xi against Wenli and made Xi acting military governor of the Chengde army.

units.zh: 及文禮誅，將正授節鉞，習不敢當其任，辭曰：「臣緣故使未葬，又無嗣息，臣合服斬縗，候臣禮制畢聽命。」
units.literal: When Wenli was executed and Xi was about to receive the formal commission of command, Xi did not dare undertake the post and declined, saying: "Because the late lord is not yet buried and there is no heir, your subject ought to wear the hemp of deepest mourning; when your subject's ritual obligations are finished I shall await orders."
units.idiomatic: After Wenli was killed, Zhuangzong was ready to grant Fu Xi the full commission, but Xi declined. "My late lord is still unburied and left no heir," he said. "I ought to wear the deepest mourning. When those rites are finished I will await your command."

units.zh: 及莊宗兼領鎮州，乃割相、衛二州置義寧軍，以習為節度使。
units.literal: When Zhuangzong also took charge of Zhen Prefecture, he carved out Xiang and Wei prefectures to establish the Yining army and made Xi its military commissioner.
units.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong also took charge of Zhenzhou, he carved out Xiang and Wei to form the Yining command and made Fu Xi its military commissioner.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.literal: Alas!
units.idiomatic: Alas!

units.zh: 孟子謂「春秋無義戰」，予亦以謂五代無全臣。
units.literal: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I likewise hold that in the Five Dynasties there were no whole ministers.
units.idiomatic: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I say the Five Dynasties knew no ministers whole in loyalty.

units.zh: 無者，非無一人，蓋僅有之耳，余得死節之士三人焉。
units.literal: “None” does not mean not a single man—it means barely any; I found three men who died for principle.
units.idiomatic: “None” is not literally none—only a handful; I count three who died for principle.

units.zh: 從葛從周攻滄州，敗劉仁恭於老鴉堤。
units.literal: Following Ge Congzhou against Cangzhou, he defeated Liu Rengong at Old Crow Embankment.
units.idiomatic: With Ge Congzhou at Cangzhou he helped defeat Liu Rengong at Old Crow Embankment.

units.zh: 還攻王熔於鎮州，入其城中，取其馬牛萬計。
units.literal: Returning to attack Wang Rong at Zhenzhou, he entered the city and took tens of thousands of horses and cattle.
units.idiomatic: Turning on Wang Rong at Zhenzhou he entered the city and took tens of thousands of horses and cattle.

units.zh: 遷宋州刺史。
units.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Song.
units.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Song.

title.raw: 卷12 孝静紀 Volume 12 Annals: (Emperor) Xiaojing

units.zh: 孝靜皇帝，諱善見，清河文宣王亶之世子也，母曰胡妃。
units.literal: Xiaojing Emperor bore the taboo name Shanjian; he was the heir of Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe, Dan; his mother was Consort Hu.
units.idiomatic: Xiaojing Emperor bore the taboo name Shanjian. He was heir to Prince Wenxuan of Qinghe, Dan; his mother was Lady Hu.

units.zh: 永熙三年，拜通直散騎侍郎，八月，為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
units.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was appointed direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; in the eighth month he was made general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division commander.
units.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he became direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; in the eighth month he was made general of agile cavalry with an opening office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

units.zh: 出帝既入關，齊獻武王奉迎不克，乃與百僚會議，推帝以奉肅宗之後，時年十一。
units.literal: When the emperor who had gone west had entered the passes, Gao Huan, Prince Xianwu of Qi went to welcome him but could not succeed; he then met with the hundred officials in council and set up the emperor to continue the line after Emperor Suzong—he was eleven years old.
units.idiomatic: After the western-departing emperor entered the passes, Gao Huan, Prince Xianwu of Qi tried to welcome him back and failed. He then convened the ministers and enthroned the boy to carry on the line of Emperor Suzong—eleven years old.

units.zh: 「務衫」不可考。
units.literal: "Service shirt" cannot be verified.
units.idiomatic: "Service shirt" cannot be verified.

units.zh: 絳衫是戎服，南齊書卷四七王融傳說他「戎服絳衫」，同書卷七一崔慧景附崔恭祖傳有「禿馬絳衫，手刺倒賊」之文。
units.literal: Crimson shirt is military dress; the Southern Qi Shu, volume 47, biography of Wang Rong, says he "wore military dress, crimson shirt," and the same book, volume 71, biography of Cui Huizong with attached biography of Cui Gongzu, has "bare horse, crimson shirt, hand stabbed the fallen bandit."
units.idiomatic: Crimson shirt is military dress; Southern Qi Shu volume 47, Wang Rong's biography, says he "wore military dress, crimson shirt," and volume 71, Cui Huizong with Cui Gongzu attached, has "bare horse, crimson shirt, hand stabbed the fallen bandit."

units.zh: 上云「從容雅服」，下自當說不得戎服，作「絳衫」似較長。
units.literal: Above it says "easy and elegant dress"; below it should speak of not being allowed military dress—"crimson shirt" seems preferable.
units.idiomatic: Above it says "easy and elegant dress"; below it should forbid military dress—"crimson shirt" seems preferable.

translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao, courtesy name Juyuan, came from Huai in Henei commandery.

units.zh: 父曜，宛句令。
units.en: His father Shan Yao had been magistrate of Yuanju.
units.literal: His father Yao was magistrate of Yuanju.

translations.literal: His father Yao was magistrate of Yuanju.
